content.text:
No, not yet. `src/services/user-service.js` still imports `query` and `update` directly from `../db.js` and uses callbacks. Line 3 even says so: "Callback-style database access. Chapter 5 migrates this to UserRepository."

`src/repositories/user-repository.js` already has the promise-based replacements. Each one runs the same query as its old counterpart:

| user-service.js (current) | UserRepository (target) |
|---|---|
| `listActiveUsers(callback)` | `findActive()` |
| `findUser(id, callback)` | `findById(id)` |
| `softDeleteUser(id, when, callback)` | `softDelete(id, when)` |

The routes are why this isn't a one-file change. `src/api/routes.js:8-9` calls `listActiveUsers` and `findUser` as callbacks, so `GET /users` and `GET /users/:id` depend on that style. Nothing in `routes.js` calls `softDeleteUser`. If the service switches to promises, either the routes have to change too, or the service needs to keep callback-style wrappers for them.

I can migrate it if you want. There's a migrate procedure under the `change-code` skill for this.
